title: The 50/30/20 Budgeting Rule
subtitle: Master a simple, intuitive framework to organize every paycheck.

steps.content: Budgeting does not mean depriving yourself. It simply gives every dollar a specific job before the month starts!
steps.tip: Track after-tax income to know your true monthly spending baseline.

steps.title: The 50/30/20 Framework
steps.content:
50% Needs: Rent, groceries, utilities, minimum debt payments, and healthcare.

30% Wants: Dining out, subscriptions, concert tickets, and vacations.

20% Savings & Debt: Emergency fund, retirement accounts, and extra debt payments.

steps.question: In the 50/30/20 budgeting rule, what should the 50% category cover?
steps.hint: The largest 50% chunk is reserved for non-negotiable living essentials that you cannot live without.

options.text: Essential needs like housing, groceries, utilities, and minimum debt payments
options.explanation: 50% covers non-negotiable living essentials that keep your life running.

options.text: Discretionary spending on dining out and hobbies
options.explanation: Dining out and hobbies belong to the 30% wants category.
Investments belong in the 20% savings category.

steps.content: The beauty of the 50/30/20 rule is that you can spend your 30% wants guilt-free because your needs and future savings are already locked in.
steps.tip: Automating your 20% savings on payday prevents accidental overspending.

steps.question: If your take-home pay is $4,000 per month, how much should go toward savings and extra debt payoff under 50/30/20?
steps.hint: Calculate 20% of the $4,000 monthly take-home pay: 0.20 × 4,000.

options.explanation: 20% of $4,000 equals $800, dedicated to emergency funds, investments, and debt elimination.
$400 is only 10%, which is below the recommended 20% target.
$1,200 represents 30%, which is the allocation for wants.

steps.title: Budgeting Framework Unlocked
steps.content: You can now split any paycheck effortlessly: 50% for Needs, 30% for Wants, and 20% for your Financial Future.
